mission.title: containerd: Default AppArmor profile denies signals inside a container when the label is stacked (`//&unconfined`, Ubuntu apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1)
mission.description: Default AppArmor profile denies signals inside a container when the label is stacked (`//&unconfined`, Ubuntu apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1). Requested by 16+ users.

steps.title: Check current containerd deployment
steps.description:
Verify your containerd version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n containerd -l app.kubernetes.io/name=containerd
helm list -n containerd 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working containerd installation.

steps.title: Review containerd configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant containerd configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n containerd -l app.kubernetes.io/name=containerd
kubectl get configmap -n containerd -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=containerd
```
On Ubuntu hosts with `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1` (the default, from `/usr/lib/sysctl.d/10-apparmor.conf` in Ubuntu's `apparmor` package), processes in a container confined by containerd's default profile can no longer signal

steps.title: Apply the fix for Default AppArmor profile denies signals inside a container…
steps.description:
Here is another investigation I have done with the help of Claude in Kubernetes context where an kernel update led to a broken Postgres and .NET runtime:

## Summary

On nodes running Ubuntu 26.04.1 with kernel `7.0.0-42-generic`, AppArmor denies
`signal` operations between processes (and threads)
```yaml
apparmor="AUDIT" operation="change_onexec" info="change_profile unprivileged unconfined converted to stacking" comm="runc:[2:INIT]" target="cri-containerd.apparmor.d//&unconfined"
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n containerd -l app.kubernetes.io/name=containerd
kubectl get events -n containerd --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Default AppArmor profile denies signals inside a container…" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
Here is another investigation I have done with the help of Claude in Kubernetes context where an kernel update led to a broken Postgres and .NET runtime:

## Summary

On nodes running Ubuntu 26.04.1 with kernel `7.0.0-42-generic`, AppArmor denies
`signal` operations between processes (and threads) of the **same container**.
codeSnippets: apparmor="AUDIT" operation="change_onexec" info="change_profile unprivileged unconfined converted to stacking" comm="runc:[2:INIT]" target="cri-containerd.apparmor.d//&unconfined"
apparmor="DENIED" operation="signal" profile="cri-containerd.apparmor.d" comm="postgres" requested_mask="send" signal=urg peer="cri-containerd.apparmor.d//&unconfined"

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with containerd installed or the issue environment reproducible.
